task_text: Goal: estimate a classifier's performance on NEW patients. Each patient has five highly correlated visits. Which pipelines are valid estimates of this goal? A: random visit split, train-only scaling, tune only on train. B: patient-group train/validation/test split, train-only fit of preprocessing and model, tune on validation, locked test once. C: patient-group split but supervised feature selection on all labels before splitting. D: patient-group split, fit on train but use test results to choose best of 20 variants and report that test. E: nested patient-group CV, preprocessing/selection/tuning all inside each outer training fold, evaluate each outer test once, no post-hoc variant choice. F: train on visits before June and test on later visits from the SAME patients. Return valid_pipeline_ids as a list, A_issue/C_issue/D_issue/F_issue chosen from patient_overlap, supervised_leakage, test_selection_bias, temporal_drift_only, none. Conditional on one visit in test in an independent 80% train /20% test visit split, return probability_patient_also_in_train using its other four visits. Is a reported increase after choosing the best of 20 test-set variants alone evidence of a genuine improvement? Return genuine_improvement_established (boolean).

response.concise_method_summary: Valid estimates of new-patient performance require that no single patient's visits appear on both sides of any split, and that no test-set information (labels, scores, or selection) influences preprocessing, feature selection, tuning, or model choice. B (group split, train-only fitting, one locked test) and E (nested group CV with all selection/tuning inside each outer training fold) satisfy both conditions. A violates patient independence via a random visit-level split. C leaks test labels into feature selection before the split. D uses test-set results to pick among 20 variants, biasing the reported number (winner's curse). F keeps the same patients in train and test despite different time windows, so it still measures within-patient generalization, not new-patient generalization; the temporal ordering is a distractor, not the primary issue. For the probability question: with an independent per-visit 80/20 assignment (each visit is train with probability 0.8, test with probability 0.2, independently), conditioning on one visit being in test leaves the other four visits independent Bernoulli(0.8) draws; the probability that at least one of them lands in train is 1 - 0.2^4 = 0.9984, confirming visits are not truly independent at the patient level even under a supposedly 'independent' split. Finally, selecting the best of 20 variants by test performance alone does not establish a genuine improvement, since repeated test-set evaluation and selection produces optimistic bias (multiple comparisons / winner's curse) absent an independent confirmation set.
assumptions: "Independent 80/20 visit split" means each visit is assigned to train or test via an independent Bernoulli(0.8/0.2) draw, not sampling without replacement to an exact ratio.

For F, patient_overlap is judged the dominant issue over temporal_drift_only because the stated goal is generalization to new patients, and F reuses the same patients in both sets regardless of time ordering.
"Patient also in train" for the probability question means at least one of the patient's other four visits lands in the train set.
Locked test set in B is evaluated only once, with no iteration back into modeling choices.
E's nested CV assumes group-aware (patient-level) folds at both outer and inner levels.
proposed_verification: Manually verify patient IDs are disjoint between train/val/test partitions in B and across outer folds in E.
Re-derive the probability via simulation: generate patients with 5 correlated visit assignments under independent Bernoulli(0.8), condition on one test visit, estimate P(any other visit in train).
Check that D's reported test metric is not reused for any further model selection or reporting decision.
Confirm C's feature selection step is refit inside each training fold only, using no test labels at any stage.
Review F's data description for whether it's the same patients across the June cutoff (confirms patient_overlap) versus disjoint patients (would make it temporal_drift_only).
